summary: NAT port reallocation during VPC egress causes SSE resume to lose terminal JSON fragment and final paragraph
description:
Issue summary: Customer reports consistent loss of the final JSON chunk and trailing paragraph when an SSE streaming response is resumed after a short network interruption that coincides with outbound VPC NAT port reallocation. Impact: Multiple user sessions at Finexa Bank observing incomplete finalization for policy-generation jobs; customers see valid-looking JSON but the last element ("conclusion") is missing and the closing metadata block is not emitted. This causes downstream parsing failures and retries in their ingestion pipeline.

Environment: Finexa Private deployment on Redwood Private (customer-managed VPC egress through NAT gateway + corporate proxy). Workload: batch policy generation using redwood/longform-v2 with streaming enabled (SSE). Frequency: ~0.6% of streams for this customer during business-hours burst (observed across three pods).

Steps to reproduce (observed pattern):
1) Client initiates SSE stream for longform generation (prompt ~1200 tokens).
2) Stream produces multiple SSE data events and partial choices; client pauses reading intermittently (backpressure) for 10–15s during model synthesis.
3) VPC NAT gateway deallocates ephemeral port due to TCP idle timeout; new outbound connection uses a different source port.
4) Edge proxy sees the connection as a new TCP flow and performs a half-close/replace sequence with backend (haproxy/nginx flow detected).
5) Client reconnects and sends a resume token; resume handshake completes but the server-side session emits the final SSE events minus a trailing JSON object containing final_choice metadata and the closing "end" event.

Observed behavior: The stream ends with a closing-brace-truncated JSON (missing final_choice array and end marker). The client receives no explicit 5xx; the stream simply stops after a short keepalive. No application-level error logged by serving-runtime except a late ACK anomaly.

Logs & artifacts attached: (embedded excerpts below)
- edge-proxy access logs: sequence of two requests ~14s apart, second with new source port and a haproxy backend-reuse flag.
- serving-runtime stdout: "WARN: resume token validated, kv-cache miss on stream 0x7f3b2e" followed by "INFO: stream closed, graceful=true" but no finalization record.
- packet capture (customer-provided tcpdump): shows TCP FIN/ACK from intermediate NAT at t=+9s, new SYN from same client at t=+11s.

Customer impact: Customers parsing generator output get a JSONDecodeError when trying to load the final chunk. Ingest retries sometimes duplicate earlier paragraphs. Business impact: delayed downstream workflows and manual reconciliation required for ~0.6% of policy jobs during spikes.

Immediate customer workaround: Requesting customer to disable client-side aggressive idle pauses and to keep SSE keepalive interval lower (10s) to avoid NAT idle deallocation. This mitigates but does not eliminate the phenomenon during heavy bursts.

Desired outcome: Ensure resume flow retains/serializes closing metadata and final_choice even when outbound source-port changes occur. If impossible, return explicit non-2xx/structured resume-failure event so clients can handle robustly.
comments: 2026-03-12 - Maya Patel: Customer first reported at 08:37 UTC. Provided tcpdump and edge proxy logs. Customer notes issue reproduces reliably when their client pauses read for >8s.

2026-03-12 - Diego Alvarez: Acknowledged; started triage. Initial hypothesis: NAT port deallocation causing backend worker to consider resumed stream as new session without re-emitting finalization. Requested customer-side keepalive settings and run trace-id-collection on next repro.

2026-03-13 - Diego Alvarez: Reproduced in private staging by simulating NAT port churn using tc/netem and an intermediate proxy. Observed identical behavior: final metadata missing and serving-runtime logs indicate 'kv-cache miss on resume' followed by 'graceful close' without finalizer hook firing. Filed INT-4082 for deeper runtime trace insertion.

2026-03-14 - SRE (Arjun Menon): Captured heap profile and enabled debug streaming traces on two affected pods. Noted resume path assumes persistent connection context; reconnect path picks up a new ephemeral session id and skips finalization when kv-cache sequence numbers mismatch.

2026-03-14 - Product (Lena Zhou): Prioritizing a guarded fix that emits an explicit SSE 'resume_failed' control event when a resume token validation succeeds but sequence reconciliation fails. Backfilling a short-term mitigation in the edge-proxy: preserve active source port mapping via connection tracking tweak for affected customers.

2026-03-14 - Diego Alvarez: Communicated mitigation to customer (edge-proxy connection-tracking change + recommended client keepalive). Customer will validate over the next 48 hours; awaiting confirmation.
investigation_notes: tcpdump indicates NAT gateway issues: FIN from NAT followed by SYN reuse, port change from 54321->60213 within 2 seconds.
Edge proxy (haproxy) shows backend reuse flag 'r' and stream-id mapping changes; backend logs show 'resume-token-valid' followed by missing finalize hook call.

Serving runtime: resume path tries to reconcile KV cache using last-seen sequence id. On mismatch, current code logs a warning but proceeds without triggering final choice aggregation; missing guard to emit an explicit error event to client.
Simulated repro in staging by artificially expiring ephemeral port and reproducing client pause; confirmed identical truncated final chunk in staging.
Related internal ticket INT-4082 created to add a resume-sequence reconciliation tracepoint and to force explicit resume-failure event emission during mismatches.

Hypothesis: When source-port changes, edge/proxy lifecycle causes worker to attach a new ephemeral stream context; resume validation succeeds superficially, but internal sequence pointers (kv-cache seq) are out-of-sync, causing final chunk to be skipped to avoid duplicate emission. Side-effect: no explicit error is returned to client.
resolution_notes: In progress: SRE applied an edge-proxy connection-tracking tweak to reduce NAT-triggered port churn for Finexa flows (rolled out 2026-03-14). Developer change under review: modify serving-runtime resume handler to emit a 'resume_failed' SSE event containing structured reason and to not silently swallow finalization when sequence reconciliation cannot be satisfied. ETA for runtime patch: 2026-03-21. Customer has agreed to temporary client keepalive adjustment as mitigation.
postmortem_followup: Add automated e2e test that simulates VPC NAT port reallocation and verifies SSE resume emits either final chunk or explicit resume_failed event.
Document recommended client keepalive guidance for Private customers behind NATs in the runbook (Confluence page linked above).
Consider conservative default: emit resume_failed control event on any resume with kv-cache sequence mismatch rather than silently continuing.
